title: CRISPR tech selectively shreds cancer cells, including "undruggable" cancers
summary: Researchers at the Innovative Genomics Institute developed a CRISPR-based technique that can selectively target and destroy cancer cells, including previously 'undruggable' cancers that resist conventional treatments. The technology leverages gene editing to precisely identify and eliminate malignant cells while sparing healthy tissue.
problem_solved: Provides a new therapeutic approach for treating cancers that have no effective drug targets, offering hope for previously untreatable malignancies.
why_valuable: This breakthrough enables selective destruction of cancer cells using precision gene editing, potentially revolutionizing oncology treatment with fewer side effects than traditional chemotherapy.
